isolation.command: docker compose --project-directory {{repoRoot}} exec -T postgres createdb -U bookshop -T bookshop {{isolationName}}
isolation.teardownCommand: docker compose --project-directory {{repoRoot}} exec -T postgres dropdb -U bookshop --if-exists {{isolationName}}

notes: createdb runs inside the running container, so no psql has to exist on the host.
Templating from the base database requires no active connections to it; when that fails the verdict falls back to REFUSE rather than writing to the shared database.

Deliberately mechanism none. SELECT isolates the keyspace but NOT pub/sub: a message published on database 10 reaches a subscriber on database 1, so channel names collide across every logical database.
Channel prefixing would be an application change, not an overlay knob. Any service that publishes here is refused unless the risk is accepted explicitly.

stateReview.notes: init_db runs CREATE TABLE on startup, so every launch is a migration against whatever database it points at.

notes: Builds from its own directory, so packages/contracts/** edits do NOT reach it — this service is deliberately absent from the shared entry's consumers.

This overlay runs in a container, so localhost would resolve to the container itself. The worktree compose file declares the base stack's network external, which keeps the base DNS names working unchanged. See references/discovery.md section 4.
verifyRequest targets localhost because curl runs on the host, where the overlay publishes its port.
Present so a shared-tree edit fans out to every service whose build context includes it.
Services building from their own directory are deliberately absent from consumers.

stateReview.notes: Browser client only: it reaches backends over HTTP and holds no store credentials, so both lists are checked-empty rather than unknown.

notes: Not dockerized. Service URLs fall back to http://localhost:PORT in code, so it reaches the base stack with no config.
cp -Rc is an APFS clone: near-instant, near-zero disk, and each server keeps its own pre-bundle cache.

constraints.where: CORS_ORIGINS, set on every service in docker-compose.yml
constraints.effect: An overlay frontend on a port outside the allowlist gets 400 with no CORS header, while /health still answers 200 — the browser only shows 'Failed to fetch'.
constraints.remedy: Have the user add the port to the gitignored root .env before launching; verify by reading the response headers of a real cross-origin request.

frontend.result: login POST returned 200 with access-control-allow-origin echoed back
